source: Show that the mean of 10, 10, 11 and 17 balances the distanc

items.question: Show that the mean of 10, 10, 11 and 17 balances the distances, and that 13 does not.
steps: Left of 12: 2 + 2 + 1 = 5. Right of 12: 17 − 12 = 5. They are equal.
Try 13. Left of 13: 3 + 3 + 2 = 8. Right of 13: 17 − 13 = 4. Not equal.
Try 11. Left of 11: 1 + 1 + 0 = 2. Right of 11: 6 + 0 = 6. Not equal.
items.answer: Only 12 balances the distances; 13 and 11 do not

source: The data 5, 5, 10, 24 has mean 11. Find the new mean after i

items.question: The data 5, 5, 10, 24 has mean 11. Find the new mean after including 17.
steps: Sum of the data = 5 + 5 + 10 + 24 = 44, and 44 ÷ 4 = 11.
New sum = 44 + 17 = 61, with 5 values.
17 is above 11, so the mean moved up, as predicted.
items.answer: The new mean is 12.2, higher than 11

videos.answer: The new mean is 12.2, higher than 11

source: The data 5, 5, 10, 24 has mean 11. Include 2 values, one 4 b

items.question: The data 5, 5, 10, 24 has mean 11. Include 2 values, one 4 below 11 and one 4 above, and check the mean is unchanged.
steps: The new values are 7 and 15.
New sum = 44 + 7 + 15 = 66, with 6 values.
New mean = 66 ÷ 6 = 11.
The deficit 4 and the surplus 4 cancel.
items.answer: The mean stays 11

videos.answer: The mean stays 11

source: The data 8, 3, 10, 13, 4, 6, 7, 7, 8, 8, 5 has 11 values. Fi

items.question: The data 8, 3, 10, 13, 4, 6, 7, 7, 8, 8, 5 has 11 values. Find its mean, then the mean when every value is increased by 10, and when every value is doubled.
steps: The mean is 79 ÷ 11 ≈ 7.18.
Every value plus 10: the mean is 7.18 + 10 = 17.18.
Every value minus 1: the mean is 7.18 − 1 = 6.18.
Every value doubled: the mean is 2 × 7.18 = 14.36.
items.answer: About 7.18, then 17.18 after adding 10, 6.18 after subtracting 1, and 14.36 after doubling

videos.answer: About 7.18, then 17.18 after adding 10, 6.18 after subtracting 1, and 14.36 after doubling

source: Use algebra to show what happens to the mean when 2 is subtr

items.question: Use algebra to show what happens to the mean when 2 is subtracted from every one of n values whose mean is a.
steps: The values are x1, x2, … xn, and (x1 + x2 + … + xn) ÷ n = a.
The new sum is (x1 − 2) + (x2 − 2) + … + (xn − 2) = x1 + x2 + … + xn − 2n.
Dividing by n gives a − 2.
items.answer: The new mean is a − 2

videos.answer: The new mean is a − 2

items.question: Find the mean of the following data and share your observations: (i) The first 50 natural numbers. (ii) The first 50 odd numbers. (iii) The first 50 multiples of 4.
steps: (i) The sum is 50 × 51 ÷ 2 = 1275, so the mean is 1275 ÷ 50 = 25.5.
(ii) The first 50 odd numbers add to 50 × 50 = 2500, so the mean is 2500 ÷ 50 = 50.
(iii) These are 4 times the natural numbers, so the mean is 4 × 25.5 = 102.
Observation: for evenly spaced values the mean is the average of the first and the last value.

items.question: The dot plot shows a collection of data and its average; but one dot is missing. Mark the missing value so that the mean is 9. The ten dots shown are at 4, 7, 8, 8, 9, 9, 9, 9, 9 and 11.
steps: Count the dots shown: 10 values, and the missing one makes 11 values.
For mean 9 the total must be 9 × 11 = 99.
The shown values add to 83, so the missing value is 99 − 83 = 16.

items.question: Shreyas measures the heights of all 24 students and finds an average of 150.2 cm. The students wore uniform shoes that add 1 cm to the height. (i) Must the heights be measured again without shoes? (ii) What is the correct average height?

items.question: Mean grids: (i) Fill a 3 by 3 grid with 9 distinct numbers so that the average along each row, column and diagonal is 10. (ii) Can we fill the grid by changing a few numbers and still get 10 as the average in all directions?
steps: An average of 10 over 3 numbers means each line adds to 30.
Start from the magic square 2, 7, 6 / 9, 5, 1 / 4, 3, 8 whose lines add to 15 and add 5 to every value. This shifts every line total by 15.
The grid is 7, 12, 11 / 14, 10, 6 / 9, 8, 13. Each row, column and both diagonals add to 30.
(ii) Yes. Swapping the grid across its main diagonal changes six cells and still gives 30 in every direction.
items.answer: 7, 12, 11 / 14, 10, 6 / 9, 8, 13 works; yes, other grids also work

videos.answer: 7, 12, 11 / 14, 10, 6 / 9, 8, 13 works; yes, other grids also work

items.question: Check whether each statement is true and justify it, using algebra if needed: (i) The average of two even numbers is even. (ii) The average of any two multiples of 5 is a multiple of 5. (iii) The average of any 5 multiples of 5 is also a multiple of 5.
steps: (i) Write the numbers as 2a and 2b. Their average is a + b, which can be odd. 2 and 4 give 3. False.
(ii) Write them as 5a and 5b. The average is 5(a + b) ÷ 2, which is not always a multiple of 5. 5 and 10 give 7.5. False.
(iii) The average of 5a, 5b, 5c, 5d, 5e is a + b + c + d + e, which need not be a multiple of 5. 5, 5, 5, 5, 10 give 6. False.
items.answer: All three statements are false

videos.answer: All three statements are false

items.question: The mean harvest of 15 trees is 25.6, but one count was written 3 more than the actual. Find the correct mean.

items.question: Find the median of 8, 10, 19, 23, 26, 34, 40, 41, 41, 48, 51, 55, 70, 84, 91, 92. (i) What value can be included without affecting the median? (ii) What two values? (iii) What one value can be removed without affecting the median?
steps: There are 16 values, so the median is the average of the 8th and 9th values 41 and 41, which is 41.
(i) Include 41. The middle value stays 41.
(ii) Include one value at most 41 and one at least 41, for example 10 and 90.
(iii) Remove one of the two 41s. The 15 values left have the 8th value as 41.
items.answer: The median is 41; add 41; add a pair like 10 and 90; remove a 41

items.question: Justify whether each statement is always true, sometimes true or never true: (i) Removing a value less than the median will decrease the median. (ii) Including a value less than the mean will decrease the mean. (iii) Including any 4 values will not affect the median. (iv) Including 4 values less than the median will increase the median.
steps: (i) Never true. The middle moves up or stays; for 1, 2, 3 removing 1 gives 2 and 3 with median 2.5.
(ii) Always true. A value below the mean adds more left distance, so the balance point moves down.
(iii) Sometimes true. Two low and two high values leave it; four high values do not.
(iv) Never true. Values below the median push it down or leave it.
items.answer: (i) never (ii) always (iii) sometimes (iv) never

videos.answer: (i) never (ii) always (iii) sometimes (iv) never

items.question: Two new students join a class whose average height was 150.2 cm with 24 students. (i) Which statements are correct? (ii) The new heights are 149 cm and 152 cm: what happens to the mean? (iii) What happens to the median?
steps: (i) The new heights have to be measured, since they decide the new average. The others claim too much.
(ii) 149 is 1.2 below 150.2 and 152 is 1.8 above. The surplus wins, so the average increases slightly: (24 × 150.2 + 149 + 152) ÷ 26 ≈ 150.22.
(iii) The median depends on the actual heights, which we are not given, so there is not enough information.

items.question: The number of times students rode their cycles in a week is shown in a dot plot. Four students rode twice. (i) Find the average number of rides. (ii) Find the median. (iii) Which statements are valid: (a) Everyone used their cycle at least once. (b) Almost everyone used their cycle a few times. (c) Some students cycled more than once on some days. (d) Exactly 5 students used their cycles more than once on some days. (e) The next week all cycled 1 more time: new average and median?
steps: The counts read from the plot: 0 rides 3 students, 1 ride 1, 2 rides 4, 3 rides 7, 4 rides 7, 5 rides 5, 6 rides 4, 7 rides 6, 8 rides 3, 10 rides 2. That is 42 students.
(ii) The 21st and 22nd values: the running totals are 3, 4, 8, 15, 22. Both are 4, so the median is 4.

(iii) (a) is not valid because 3 students rode 0 times. (b) is valid: 39 of 42 rode at least once. (c) is valid: someone who rode 8 or 10 times in a week must have ridden twice on a day. (d) is valid: exactly 3 + 2 = 5 students rode more than 7 times.
(e) Every value goes up by 1, so the mean becomes about 5.6 and the median 5.
items.answer: (i) about 4.6 (ii) 4 (iii) (b), (c), (d) are valid (e) about 5.6 and 5

videos.answer: (i) about 4.6 (ii) 4 (iii) (b), (c), (d) are valid (e) about 5.6 and 5

items.question: The average number of customers visiting a shop and actually purchasing items over the week is given: Mon to Sun visiting 16, 19, 10, 14, 20, 22, 35 and purchasing 10, 8, 7, 11, 12, 16, 26. Visualise this data on a line graph.

items.question: A table gives the retail price in rupees of iodised salt in January over 10 years, 2016 to 2025, for Andaman and Nicobar Islands, Assam, Gujarat, Mizoram, Uttar Pradesh and West Bengal. (i) Show any 3 states as a line graph with a suitable scale. (ii) What do you find interesting? (iii) Compare the price variation in Gujarat and Uttar Pradesh. (iv) In which state did the price rise the most from 2016 to 2025? (v) What are you curious to explore further?
steps: (i) Years 2016 to 2025 along the bottom; prices from 0 to 30 rupees up the side in steps of 5, with one line per state.
(iii) Gujarat stays near 14 to 15 rupees for most years and jumps to 19.2 only in 2025. Uttar Pradesh climbs steadily from 16.15 to 26.9 and then dips to 24.81, so it varies much more.

(iv) Rise from 2016 to 2025: Andaman and Nicobar Islands 20.99 − 16 = 4.99, Assam 12.35 − 6 = 6.35, Gujarat 19.2 − 16.5 = 2.7, Mizoram 29.8 − 20 = 9.8, Uttar Pradesh 24.81 − 16.15 = 8.66, West Bengal 23.99 − 9.47 = 14.52. The biggest rise is in West Bengal.
(ii) and (v) are open: for example, why West Bengal's price rose from 9.47 to 23.99, and whether the same happens with other food items.
items.answer: West Bengal rose the most, by about 14.52 rupees; Gujarat varied less than Uttar Pradesh

videos.answer: West Bengal rose the most, by about 14.52 rupees; Gujarat varied less than Uttar Pradesh

source: Mumbai's rain peaks in July and Chennai's in November. Which

items.question: Mumbai's rain peaks in July and Chennai's in November. Which monsoon brings each peak?
steps: The south west monsoon reaches the west coast from June to September, which covers July.
The north east monsoon reaches the south east coast in October to December, which covers November.
So Mumbai's peak comes from the south west monsoon and Chennai's from the north east monsoon.
items.answer: Mumbai: south west monsoon; Chennai: north east monsoon

items.question: On a 3 by 3 Hex board the players fill all 9 cells. Can the game end with neither player joining their two sides?
steps: Try filling a small board in every way you can: one colour always joins its two sides.
